retry_at.description: When a retry's backoff ends, if known.

and checked there. Land only fast-forwards the base from `base_tip` to `head`. Absent from

The current round of Land, from its first step until the next exit choice opens.

shapes.description: `tool`, `ask` and/or `react`, for the lines the extension configures.

Every parent's full commit ID in Git's order (first parent first). A parent need not
be on this page: it is further down the walk, never a root.

refs.description: Local branches (`main`), tags (`tag: v1`) and `HEAD` that point at this commit.

refs_omitted.description: Ref labels at this commit beyond those listed (at most 16 are).

GitHistoryPage.description:
A page of commits reachable from one tip, children before parents (`git log --topo-order`).

The first page (no `DetailGet.page`) resolves the ref; every later page walks from the same
`tip`, so a walk is a stable snapshot even when the ref moves. Asking for the first page
again is the refresh: a moved ref changes its `tip` and etag.

Some commit is named by more records than one read takes (or the daemon could not look
records up by commit), so links may be missing.

reference.description: The fully qualified ref read (`refs/heads/main`), or `HEAD` for the project checkout's.

refs_incomplete.description: The ref listing hit its bound, so any commit may lack some of its labels.

skip.description: Commits already walked before this page.

tip.description: Full commit ID the walk starts from; absent when the ref has no commits yet.

The worker run submitted this commit for review (a recorded submission, or its current
head when it has not landed). The run may have landed a different, rebased commit.

The reviewer run was bound to this candidate when a verdict on it was recorded; the
verdict may have been the owner's. Not served: no record names its project.

name.description: Exact key in the effective engine harness configuration.

resolved_path.description: Executable file observed on the daemon host, not a guarantee of what a runner launches.

ready.description: Whether the pipeline appended `ready` for the current review.

recovery_session.description: Ended run eligible for explicit session.relaunch after session loss.

resolved_profile.description: Worker profile dispatch would select without an explicit override.

reviewer.description: Live reviewer session, even when `run` holds the worker.

TerminalColor.description:
A terminal colour: an index into the 256-colour palette (0-15 are the client's theme
colours), or a 24-bit `[red, green, blue]`.

TerminalRun.description:
Consecutive cells of one terminal row that share a style. An absent colour is the terminal's
default for that ground; the client owns the defaults and the indexed palette.

inverse.description: Foreground and background swapped (SGR 7), resolved by the client against its defaults.

lines.description:
Latest bounded scrollback plus screen, in display order. Stream pages replace this
window, never append repeated screen rows. Recorded gates remain non-live captures.

rows.description:
The same lines as styled runs, one row per line, when the source carries styling (a live
pane's screen); empty otherwise. A row's run texts concatenate to its line.

tasks.description:
The tasks named by the window's runs and events, their ancestors (up to eight parent
hops), and the direct children of those window tasks and their immediate parents.
Also includes one level of dependencies from that set. Absent from an older daemon.

TimelineTask.description: What the Timeline needs of one task; never its body.

landed.description:
When the task last landed, from the whole event log (not only the window). Absent
unless the task is currently Done and has a landing without a later `reopened` event.

parent.description: The plan this task belongs to.

oneOf.description: Project fact observations (`system.v1`).
Shared rows for clients granted `assistant.v1` or `build.v1`.
Daemon-host performance (`host.v1`), one row, host-wide.

TranscriptOp.description:
One operation on the tail of a session's transcript, for a `session.transcript.v1`
client. Applied in order to the messages the client holds, the operations give the
transcript's current branch up to the present, the message being written included, so
such a client never reads `detail.get { session }` again to follow a turn.

oneOf.description:
What the client holds no longer continues into what follows: the first page of a
subscription, another branch, a replaced journal, or a client that fell behind. The
`put`s after it are the newest messages; `older` is the `detail.get` page before the
first of them. A client that holds that first message keeps what it holds before it.

The message with this id: in place of the held message with the same id, or of the
open message `replaces` whose record it is, or else at the end. Journal records
occupy separate messages, including tool results.

before.description:
The `detail.get` page before this message; absent when nothing precedes it or
the message is open.

cut.description:
Only the last items of a record too large for one operation: `before` resumes
inside it, and the client holds nothing before this message until it pages back.

open.description:
Still being written: it has no record yet, its id names no record, and `append`s
to it follow.

oneOf.description:
Words of the open message `id`, at a UTF-8 byte offset of its one `text` or
`thinking` item, which the first chunk makes (thinking goes before text). Writing a
chunk at its offset is idempotent.
The open message `id` ended without a record.

days.description: Ascending days, including days without any reports or runs.

schema.description: Content fingerprint of the returned file; not a write precondition.
Literal text, delivered before any keys, without implicitly submitting it.

Current fleet replacement for capable clients; omission means no current fleet,
except on a page of transcript operations alone (no events, no gap), which says
nothing about the fleet.

anyOf.description: A health page contains the single current snapshot.

schema.description: Complete bounded replacement window; absent on an unavailable pane.

Replacement for capable clients on the first page, after discontinuity, or when
changed since the last page. Omission means unchanged.

Operations on the transcript's tail, in order, for `session.transcript.v1`
clients only.

anyOf.description: The head's map level and entry point scope; the project level when absent.
Optional case-insensitive filename substring, within this directory only.
Whitespace-separated words, all of which must match.
Lens ID, or its exact repository-relative file path (e.g. for a malformed file).

schema.description: Maximum result count, from 1 to `SESSION_FILE_SEARCH_LIMIT_MAX` inclusive.
Byte position, a multiple of `SESSION_HTML_CHUNK_BYTES`. Start at zero.
Nonempty UTF-8 text, at most `SESSION_FILE_SEARCH_QUERY_MAX_BYTES` bytes, no controls.
Omit for the first read. Echo the returned revision for subsequent reads.
IANA time zone name for local day boundaries, including clock changes.

anyOf.description: Exclusive local date; a range may span at most 366 days.

schema.description: Fixed minutes east of UTC (`-1439..=1439`), used when no zone is given.
If present, cancel only this turn.
Sender-chosen input ID: `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,80}`.
At most `crate::assistant::MESSAGE_TEXT_MAX` bytes.
`<provider>/<model>`.
Full model ID (`<provider>/<model>`) shown for this approval.
`<provider>/<model>`, as `ModelChoice::id`.
Ordered list of `<provider>/<model>` routes.
Use the existing checkout and its current branch instead of a new worktree.
`<provider>/<model>`; absent means the configured build route.
The host slugs the name or chooses one when absent.
A `[build.profiles]` name. Explicit fields override the profile.
A configured project; absent means the workspace root's repository.
A configured project whose checkout the trusted Code session runs in.
Resume strictly after this canonical device ID.
At most DEVICE_PAGE_LIMIT_MAX; replies also obey APP_CONTROL_MAX.
